body.text: Kauśikaprajñāpāramitāsūtram |
body.translated_text: <s>Kauśikaprajñāpāramitāsūtra</s> (The Sūtra on the Perfection of Wisdom for <s>Kauśika</s>)

body.text: namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ ||

evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamanekaiśca bodhisattvaśatasahasraiḥ sarvaiḥ kumārabhūtaiḥ | tatra khalu bhagavān śakraṃ devānāmindramāmantrayate sma ||
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) mountain, together with a great assembly of monks and with many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, all in the stage of princes (<s>kumārabhūta</s>). There, the <s>Bhagavat</s> addressed <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods:

body.text: ayaṃ kauśika prajñāpāramitāyāḥ arthaḥ - prajñāpāramitā na dvayena draṣṭavyā na advayena | na nimittato na animittataḥ | na āyūhato na nirāyūhataḥ | notkṣepato na prakṣepataḥ | na saṃkleśato na asaṃkleśataḥ | na vyavadānato na avyavadānataḥ | notsargato na anutsargataḥ | na sthānato na asthānataḥ | na yogato na ayogataḥ | na saṃbandhato na asaṃbandhataḥ | na pratyayato na apratyayataḥ | na dharmato na adharmataḥ | na tathata(yā) na atathata(yā) na bhūtakoṭyā na abhūtakoṭyā(vedi)tavyā ||
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Kauśika</s>, is the meaning of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom): the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is not to be seen through duality nor through non-duality; not through marks nor through marklessness; not through purposeful accumulation nor through non-accumulation; not through acceptance nor through rejection; not through defilement nor through non-defilement; not through purification nor through non-purification; not through relinquishment nor through non-relinquishment; not through abiding nor through non-abiding; not through conjunction nor through non-conjunction; not through connection nor through non-connection; not through condition nor through non-condition; not through <s>dharma</s> (phenomena) nor through non-<s>dharma</s>; it is to be known neither through <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) nor through non-suchness, neither through the <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (limit of reality) nor through the non-limit of reality.

body.text: evamevāyaṃ sa kauśika prajñāpāramitāyāḥ arthaḥ | tadyathā sarvadharmasamatvāt prajñāpāramitā samā | sarvadharmaviviktatvāt prajñāpāramitā viviktā | sarvadharmācalatvāt prajñāpāramitā acalā | sarvadharmāmanyatvāt prajñāpāramitā amanyatā | sarvadharmābhīrutvāt prajñāpāramitā abhīru | sarvadharmācchambhitatayā prajñāpāramitā acchambhī | sarvadharmaikarasatvāt prajñāpāramitā ekarasā | sarvadharmānutpādatvāt prajñāpāramitā anutpādā | sarvadharmānirodhatvāt prajñāpāramitā anirodhā | gaganakalpatvāt sarvadharmāṇāṃ prajñāpāramitā gaganakalpā | rūpāparyantatvāt prajñāpāramitā aparyantā | evaṃ vedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāparyantatvāt prajñāpāramitā aparyantā | pṛthivīdhātvaparyantatvāt prajñāpāramitā aparyantā | evamabdhātu - tejodhātu - vāyudhātu - ākāśadhātu - vijñānadhātvaparyantatvāt prajñāpāramitā aparyantā | sumervaparyantatvāt prajñāpāramitā aparyantā | samudrāparyantatvāt prajñāpāramitā aparyantā | vajrasamatvāt prajñāpāramitā samā | sarvadharmābhedatvāt prajñāpāramitā abhedā | sarvadharma(svabhāvā)nupalabdhitvāt prajñāpāramitā anupalabdhiḥ | sarvadharmavibhāva(nā) - samatvāt prajñāpāramitā(a)vibhāva(nā) - samā | sarvadharmaniśceṣṭatvāt prajñāpāramitā niśceṣṭā | sarvadharmācintyatvāt prajñāpāramitā acintyeti ||
body.translated_text: Thus indeed, O <s>Kauśika</s>, this is the meaning of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>. That is to say: because all <s>dharmas</s> are equal, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is equal; because all <s>dharmas</s> are isolated, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is isolated; because all <s>dharmas</s> are immovable, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is immovable; because all <s>dharmas</s> are free from conceit, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is free from conceit; because all <s>dharmas</s> are fearless, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is fearless; because all <s>dharmas</s> are unafraid, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unafraid; because all <s>dharmas</s> are of one taste, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is of one taste; because all <s>dharmas</s> are unproduced, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unproduced; because all <s>dharmas</s> are unceased, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unceased; because all <s>dharmas</s> are like space, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is like space; because <s>rūpa</s> (form) is without limit, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is without limit; likewise, because <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are without limit, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is without limit; because the earth element is without limit, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is without limit; likewise, because the water element, fire element, wind element, space element, and consciousness element are without limit, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is without limit; because <s>Sumeru</s> is without limit, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is without limit; because the ocean is without limit, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is without limit; because [all <s>dharmas</s>] are like a <s>vajra</s> (diamond/thunderbolt) in equality, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is equal; because all <s>dharmas</s> are undivided, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is undivided; because the own-nature of all <s>dharmas</s> is unobtainable, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is unobtainment; because the analysis of all <s>dharmas</s> is equal, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is equal in non-analysis; because all <s>dharmas</s> are without activity, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is without activity; because all <s>dharmas</s> are inconceivable, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is inconceivable.

body.text: evaṃ dānapāramitā - śīlapāramitā - kṣāntipāramitā - vīryapāramitā - dhyānapāramitā - prajñāpāramitātrimaṇḍalapariśuddhyaparyantatvāt prajñāpāramitā aparyantā iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus, because the purity of the three spheres (<s>trimaṇḍalapariśuddhi</s>) of the <s>Dānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Generosity), <s>Śīlapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Morality), <s>Kṣāntipāramitā</s> (Perfection of Patience), <s>Vīryapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Vigor), <s>Dhyānapāramitā</s> (Perfection of Meditation), and <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) is without limit, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is without limit.

body.text: prajñāpāramitā ucyate yaduta aṣṭādaśaśūnyatā | tadyathā - ādhyātmaśūnyatā bahirdhāśūnyatā ādhyātmābahirdhāśūnyatā śūnyatāśūnyatā mahāśūnyatā paramā(rtha)śūnyatā saṃskṛtaśūnyatā asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā atyantaśūnyatā anādyagraśūnyatā (ana)pakāraśūnyatā prakṛtiśūnyatā svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā sarvadharmaśūnyatā anupalambhaśūnyatā abhāvaśūnyatā svabhāvaśūnyatā abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā iti | ayamucyate saṃkṣiptena prajñāpāramiteti ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is called the eighteen <s>śūnyatās</s> (emptinesses). That is to say: <s>ādhyātmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal), <s>bahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the external), <s>ādhyātmabahirdhāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the internal and external), <s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of emptiness), <s>mahāśūnyatā</s> (great emptiness), <s>paramārthaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the ultimate), <s>saṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the conditioned), <s>asaṃskṛtaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the unconditioned), <s>atyantaśūnyatā</s> (absolute emptiness), <s>anādyagraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of beginninglessness and endlessness), <s>anapakāraśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-rejection), <s>prakṛtiśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of nature), <s>svalakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-characteristics), <s>sarvadharmaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of all dharmas), <s>anupalambhaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-apprehension), <s>abhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of non-being), <s>svabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of own-being), and <s>abhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the own-being of non-being). This is called, in brief, the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.text:
) tārakā timiraṃ dīpo māyāvaśyāya buddhudam |
supinaṃ vidyudabhraṃ ca evaṃ draṣṭavya saṃskṛtamiti ||
children.translated_text:
A star, a visual distortion, a lamp, an illusion, dew, a bubble,
a dream, lightning, a cloud — thus should conditioned things be viewed.
Without cessation, without arising, without annihilation, without permanence,
without a single meaning, without diverse meanings, without coming, without going —
he who taught <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), the auspicious pacification of conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañcopaśama</s>),
to that Perfectly Awakened One, the foremost of speakers, I pay homage.

body.text: namo daśasu dikṣu sarveṣāmatītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ trayāṇāṃ ratnānām | namo bhagavatyai prajñāpāramitāyai sarvatathāgatasunibhāyai sarvatathāgatānujñātavijñātāyai |(oṃ) prajñe mahāprajñe prajñāvabhāse prajñālokakāri ajñānavidhamane siddhe susiddhe siddhyamane(bha)gavate sarvāṅgasundari(bha)ktivatsale prasārahaste samāśvāsakare sidhya sidhya, budhya budhya, kampa kampa, cala cala, rāva rāva, āgaccha bhagavate mā vilamba svāhā ||
namo dharmodgatasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya mahākāruṇakasya ||

namo prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - munidharme saṃgrahadharme anugrahadharme vimokṣadharme sattvānugrahadharme vaiśramaṇadharme samantanuparivartanadharme guṇigrahasaṃgrahadharme sarvatrānugatadharme sarvakālaparipūrṇadharme svāhā ||
namo prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - akhane nikhane mukhana nekhane(avaravandane) paṭane paṭane paṭare svāhā ||
namo prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - gaṅgā gaṅgā na tīrāvabhāsa gaṅgā svāhā ||
namo prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā śrīye śrīye muni śrīye śrīyase svāhā ||
namo prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - oṃ vajrabale svāhā ||
namo prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - oṃ hrī śrī dhī śruti smṛti mati gati vijaye svāhā ||
namo prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - bambari bambari mahābambari būru būru mahābūru svāhā ||
namaḥ prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - hūte hūte hūvitāśane sarva - karmāvaraṇane svāhā
|| namaḥ prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - oṃ orolik svāhā ||
namo prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - oṃ sarvavit svāhā ||
namaḥ prajñāpāramitāyai | tadyathā - gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā ||
idamavocadbhagavān | āttamanā āyuṣmān sāriputraḥ śakro devānāmindraste ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣad sadevagandharvamānuṣāsuraśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan ||
kauśikanāma prajñāpāramitā samāptā ||
